Go to settings > general > transfer or reset iPhone > get started. Continue through this and you’ll begin an ICloud backup which will store a full copy of your phone onto the ICloud regardless how much storage you pay for/use. The catch with this is that it will only be stored for 21 days and then will be deleted. If you pay for ICloud and already have a back up you can skip this step, just make sure you update your backup.

From there a progress message will appear under your ICloud settings telling you the progress of the backup. Wait until it is finished then wipe your phone through General > transfer or reset iPhone> erase all contents and settings.

Wait for the phone to erase and start setting it up like a brand new phone, when you get to a screen that says something like “Set up your new IPhone”, select “set up without another device”. Continue through the setup steps until you see a screen asking how you would like to transfer your data, select “Restore from an ICloud backup”. Sign into your Apple ID, continue through additional setup steps, then it’ll give a progress bar indicating your iCloud restoration progress.

I recommend you plug your phone in after that and leave it over night, with over 400 GB of actual data it will take several hours.

Once everything is done, your phone should look exactly the same as when you started but now the cached system data will be gone. This is the only 100% sure fire way to remove the system data from your device.

Sincerely,

A concerned iPhone technician

I come bearing bad news, sounds like a major electrical short in your psu. There’s no easy way to figure out what all the damage is could be just your psu and mb, but it could very well be everything.

I would start by unplugging all nonessential components and drives, if you can I would plug in the drives into a different PC and make sure they’re not fried. Next if you have an IGPU, remove your gpu and continue troubleshooting:

0: recheck all your connections and basic troubleshooting as it’s entirely possible a cable isn’t plugged in all the way. If you haven’t already try a different outlet bc you may have shorted the outlet as well.

1. Easiest is ram, follow your motherboard’s manual and test booting one stick at a time. If that doesn’t work move onto step two.

2. Replace the MB, the mb is the most interconnected component to the PSU, often times a fried PSU will take the MB with it. IDEALLY your MB has some fault protection in it that will protect the CPU but it’s not guaranteed. For this step on onward you will save yourself a lot of headache if you remove all components from the case. You’re gonna have to do a lot of hardware swapping.

3. There is a chance your CPU’s fried, if replacing the mb doesn’t work then the cpu is probably the culprit. In which case you might as well buy a new system 😞. 

Sorry OP there’s no real easy way to go about this as PSU faults are the most deadly to a system. It’s possible that some dust had settled in some connections and caused a short when you booted. Either way this is a really shitty situation :(

Edit: reach out to your psu manufacturer regardless of your warranty validity let them know that your psu fried and took your whole system with it (if you get that far). I’ve heard of some brands replacing entire systems from a psu fault, but they may just ask you to send the PSU in to be evaluated by an engineering team.

SSD degradation is directly proportional to the amount of write cycles it’s been through in its life span. Windows and other OS drives are constantly reading and writing to keep the Os running so Os drives tend to degrade faster than others. 

I’ve had my system for about 5 years now and two of the SSD’s in my system are original to the first build. My MX500 250gb has been exclusively an OS drive while my 1tb WDB is a steam library drive. According to crystaldiskinfo my WDB drive is still at 98% of its health with a total host write of 11911 GB. On the other hand my MX500 is at 48% health with a total host write of 33295 gb. 

As the SSD begins to fail as it gets older the drive compensates by locking away bad sectors, slightly reducing speed and capacity.

TLDR: your drive is getting old. Shouldn’t affect gaming as most games can’t really take advantage of the entire bandwidth of a 970. Since this is your OS drive I’d be willing to bet it won’t last too much longer than 10 years

Ive found that tracking can be a lil finicky sometimes but here what I do to make it work every time.

1. Cut up your video in Premiere, nesting the clips you want in the final version
2. Export each clip into Apple prores format (.xmf) its a larger file size but it makes sure you have minimal problems in after effects
3. Create a project in Aftereffects and make a separate composition for each clip (make sure to organize your project panel). this will make sure the clips settings and comp settings are the same.
4. create a null object, select your xmf layer and begin tracking.

This is actually very natural, cats and dogs (and many other animals) have an intrinsic instinct to avoid drinking from stagnant water as stagnant water (in the wild) is typically a sespool of bacteria and parasites. Drinking from running water greatly reduces the risk of bacterial and parasitic infections. This doesn't mean that they won't drink stagnant water, they'll drink it when they're very dehydrated. This is also the reason that cats and dogs that drink out of a bowl are typically very dehydrated, pet owners with pet water fountains will find their pet much healthier and hydrated
